# Systemix

Systemix keeps your design system from rotting. It watches what you ship,
catches where design and code drift apart, proposes a fix with AI, you approve
it, and it remembers the reason — so your system gets sharper every release
instead of decaying.

## What it is

- A CLI and framework that runs a ship → signal → decide → record loop on your
  design system. Every decision and experiment is a plain MDX file in your repo
  (hypothesis, evidence, decision, confidence), written back when the loop closes.
- Three doors into the same loop: Claude Code slash-command skills, the
  `systemix` CLI, or an MCP connector (`experiment_*` tools).
- Engine = your AI coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex). No extra service,
  no local model, no platform. The files are yours.
- Ghost mode by default: it suggests, never touches your code. Autonomy dials
  up to assisted or autonomous; a human always closes the decision.
- Evidence via PostHog (optional): wire it and headlines, CTAs, and flows
  become measurable evidence. The loop runs without it.
- Code-first tokens: CSS is the source of truth; a drift report shows where
  design and code split. Figma is an optional adapter.

## Getting started

- Free: `npx systemix init` scaffolds the loop (and optionally a design system)
  in your repo, ghost mode on.
- AI Kit ($249, pay once): the full loop pre-wired — signals hookup, drift
  audit, human-approval rail, scheduled runner. Lifetime updates, no
  subscription. https://getsystemix.vercel.app/kit
- Free audit: send a repo URL, get back a drift report + top 3 proposed
  decisions. https://getsystemix.vercel.app/audit
